re: false deaths: capture loop, unvalidated hpSvc
body:
Your diagnosis is better than mine and is accepted: the invented deaths come from the CAPTURE loop, not the vanish loop (65 host DEATH, all distinct, only 6 overlap the 6 real kills, and they fire before the vanished line). Cause: cached hpSvc read without validation; a scene change recycles the address; +0x5C reads 0xFFFF and the watcher calls it a death. The '[Net] scene change ... peerKey=FFFFFFFF' prefix on every cluster is the smoking gun.

APPLY THE PATCH. Do not wait for further approval. Requirements, all of them:

1. Validate the service before any read: readable(hpSvc, 0x70) AND *(uint32_t*)hpSvc == 0x02712F60 (CSrvNPCHealth). The constant is already used elsewhere in phase1.cpp; reuse it, do not inline a magic number twice.
2. Do not trust a cached hpSvc across a scene change. Clear or re-resolve the cache on '[Net] scene change' (the same event that invalidates it). Clearing is cheaper and correct.
3. Require the transition, not the value: death is only when the SAME objId was seen in the previous capture with life in [1, maxLife] and is now 0xFFFF (or the entity is gone with the dead bit set on a VALIDATED service). A first-seen entity at 0xFFFF is not an event.
4. Emit at most once per objId, then tombstone it so a late frame cannot re-emit.
5. Keep 'merely left the radius' silent. That is the whole point of the watcher.
6. Also dedupe the apply re-push: 6 kills produced 12 '[Kill] push' lines. Use s_inEventLoop (already exists) or a per-tick set.

ACCEPTANCE (this is what I will check): a 10-minute run that crosses at least 3 streaming boundaries (walk 200 m out, come back) produces ZERO 'host DEATH' for any objId whose last observed life was in [1, maxLife]. F2 kills must still be 6/6 with non-zero objId, and '[Kill] push' must equal the number of kills, not twice it.

Report: commit, the before/after counts (vanished / host DEATH / invented), and the audit gate line. One commit.
